class epipy:
    """
    EPIPY: Mk.II.II.beta
    3DRISM interface ,water placement and data manipulation tool

    class is initialized with a solute structure file and its corresponding topology

    Parameters
    ----------
    :param solute_structure: .gro, .pdb or .xtc file
    :param solute_topology: .top or .solte file
    :param gen_idc: generate an ion-dipole-correction (IDC) enabled .solute file
      this file will be used for the remainder of the calculation
    :param convert: convert solute_topology to .solute file
    """
    def __init__(self,solute_structure:str,solute_topology:str,to_gro:bool=False,gen_idc:bool=False,
                 convert:bool=False):
      """
      class is initialized with a solute structure file and its corresponding topology
      +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
      Parameters
      ----------
      :param solute_structure: .gro, .pdb or .xtc file
      :param solute_topology: .top or .solte file
      :param gen_idc: generate an ion-dipole-correction (IDC) enabled .solute file
      this file will be used for the remainder of the calculation
      :param convert: convert solute_topology to .solute file
      """
      self.cmd_path = "" #path to eprism command
      self.grid = [] # number of grids per unit cell LxWxH
      self.closure = 'PSE3'
      #self.path = "" not sure why i added this
      self.ndiis = 5
      self.solute_path = ""
      self.solvent_path = ""#~/EPISOL-1.1.326/solvent/"
      self.r_c = 1
      self.coulomb = 'coulomb'
      self.delvv = 0.5
      self.dynamic_delvv = 1
      self.err_tol = 1e-08
      self.T = 298
      self.log = ''#'episol_out.log'
      self.threads = threading.active_count()
      self.rism_args = str()
      self.test_args = str()
      self.rism_cmd = str()
      #self.out_file = self.log#str()
      self.get_eprism_path = ''.join([chr(i) for i in subprocess.check_output(['whereis eprism3d'],shell=True)[:-1]]).split()[1][:-8]
      ## initialize solute and solvent right at the begining
      # you can do this later on if you want to change files
      self.solute(solute_structure,solute_topology,to_gro,gen_idc,convert)
      self.solvent()
      # here we set the default report name to the solute structure file name
      # and the default save to output ALL values in the log, there is no reason
      # not to do this as it is like 2 lines of text
      self.rism(step=500,resolution=1,values_to_save='all')
      # replace self.report(out_file_name=f'{self.structure_file[:-4]}_out',args=('all'))
      self.report() #out_file_name=self.structure_file,to_report='all')
      ####################################################################################
      # HERE I AM MOVING THIS TO __INIT__
      ####################################################################################

    def solute(cls,solute_structure:str,solute_topology:str,to_gro:bool=False,gen_idc:bool=False,convert:bool=False):
        """
        Read in solute structure and topology file.
        These files will be used for the remainer of the class
        :param solute_structure: .gro, .pdb or .xtc
        :param solute_topology: .top or .solute
        :param gen_idc: generate an ion-dipole-correction (IDC) enabled .solute
        this file will be used for the remainder of the
        :param convert: convert solute_topology to .solute
        """
        from os.path import basename, abspath,splitext

        # get file names and paths
        # using abspath
        try:
            cls.structure_file = basename(solute_structure)
            cls.solute_path = abspath(solute_structure).split(cls.structure_file)[0]
            cls.solute_top = basename(solute_topology)
            cls.solute_top_path = abspath(solute_topology).split(cls.solute_top)[0]
        except FileNotFoundError as exc:
            print("# ERROR ERROR ERROR ERROR ERROR\n")
            print("# Using tilde ( ~ ) for /home/user/ often breaks")
            print("# on distributed systems and/or weird places")
            print("# just write the full path ")
            print("# ERROR ERROR ERROR ERROR ERROR\n")
            raise exc

        # get uh, file extensions
        cls.structure_file_type = splitext(solute_structure)[-1]
        cls.structure_top_file_type = splitext(solute_topology)[-1]
        #
        if gen_idc:
            convert = True

        if convert:
            subprocess.run([f"gmxtop2solute -p { cls.solute_path+ cls.solute_top} -o { cls.solute_top[:-4]}.solute"],shell=True)
            print(f"converted { cls.solute_top} to { cls.solute_top[:-4]}.solute")
            cls.solute_top = f"{ cls.solute_top[:-4]}.solute"
            """ We will reset our path since we just wrote a new fle to the current dir"""
            cls.solute_top_path = ''
        if gen_idc:
            #subprocess.run([f"{ cls.get_eprism_path}generate-idc.sh { cls.solute_top[:-4]}.solute > idc_{ cls.solute_top[:-4]}.solute"],shell=True)
            subprocess.run([f"generate-idc.sh { cls.solute_top} > idc_{ cls.solute_top}"],shell=True)
            cls.solute_top = f'idc_{ cls.solute_top}'
            print(f"generated idc-enabled solute file to: { cls.solute_top}")
            """ We will reset our path since we just wrote a new fle to the current dir"""
            cls.solute_top_path = ''

        #if f"{  cls.solute_path+ cls.structure_file}"[-3:] == 'pdb':
        if cls.structure_file_type == ".pdb":
          # cls.file_type = 'pdb'
          with open(f"{cls.solute_path+ cls.structure_file}",'r') as sol:
              for line in sol:
                tmp = line.split()
                if tmp[0] == "CRYST1":
                  cls.solute_box = [tmp[1],tmp[2],tmp[3]]
                  break
          sol.close()

        #elif f"{ cls.solute_path+ cls.structure_file}"[-3:] == 'gro':
        if cls.structure_file_type == ".gro":
            # cls.file_type = 'gro'
            """
            read last line and get box vectors
            HELP FROM:
            https://stackoverflow.com/questions/3346430/
            what-is-the-most-efficient-way-to-get-first-and-last-line-of-a-text-file/18603065#18603065
            """
            import os
            try:
                with open(f"{cls.solute_path+cls.structure_file}",'rb') as f:
                    try:
                        f.seek(-2, os.SEEK_END)
                        while f.read(1) != b'\n':
                            f.seek(-2, os.SEEK_CUR)
                    except OSError:
                        f.seek(0)
                    last_line = f.readline().decode()
                f.close() #just in case
                # returns the last line in the .gro file
                cls.solute_box = [float(val) for val in last_line.split()]
            except FileNotFoundError as exc:
                print("ERROR ERROR ERROR ERROR ERROR\n")
                print("Using tilde ( ~ ) for /home/user/ often breaks")
                print("on distributed systems and/or weird places")
                print("just write the full path ")
                print("ERROR ERROR ERROR ERROR ERROR\n")
                raise exc

    def solvent(cls,solvent_topology:str=None):
        """
        Reads the solvent topology file.
        If no file specified, will default search
        the site-packages dir where episol.epipy is
        stored. this may fail as the os package sometimes
        encounters errors

        :param solvent_topology: solvent correlation file
        see EPISOL documentation for format.
        if solvent topology is set to None i.e. has no input
        then we will select the tip3p 0.01A file from the source directory
        of EPIPY, this way to avoid annoying paths.
        Solvent w
        """
        from os.path import dirname
        from inspect import getfile
        from os.path import basename, abspath,splitext

        # here we will set the solvent topology default to search the
        # site-packages directory. this way not as troublesome
        if not solvent_topology:
            cls.solvent_top ='tip3p-amber14.01A.gaff'
            cls.solvent_path = f'{dirname(getfile(epipy))}/solvents/'
        else:
            #cls.solvent_path = f'{dirname(getfile(epipy))}/solvents/'
            if solvent_topology.lower() == "mg":
                cls.solvent_path = f'{dirname(getfile(epipy))}/solvents/'
                cls.solvent_top = "tip3p-MgCl-amber18-full.gaff"
            elif solvent_topology.lower() == "water":
                cls.solvent_top = 'tip3p-amber14.01A.gaff'
                cls.solvent_path = f'{dirname(getfile(epipy))}/solvents/'
            else:
                # get file names and paths
                # using abspath
                try:
                    cls.solvent_top = basename(solvent_topology)
                    cls.solvent_path = abspath(solvent_topology).split(cls.solvent_top)[0]
                except FileNotFoundError as exc:
                    print("ERROR ERROR ERROR ERROR ERROR\n")
                    print("Using tilde ( ~ ) for /home/user/ often breaks")
                    print("on distributed systems and/or weird places")
                    print("just write the full path ")
                    print("ERROR ERROR ERROR ERROR ERROR\n")
                    raise exc

    def rism(cls,step:int=500,resolution:float=1,values_to_save:str='all',*args):
        """
        Sets the steps and resolution of the calculation.
        Will automatically set number of grids based on the box dimensions
        acquired from cls.solute()

        :param step: int(), Number of SCF steps to perform
        :param resolution: grid resolution of box (will override if previously set)
        :param values_to_save: values to save to the dump file; options below:
            * all : reports all of the below
            * command : save the exact command that was run when the file was produced
            * guv : g(r) foreach grid point
            * ld : smoothed g(r)  i.e. g(r) convolved with kernel
            * coul : coulombic potential at each grid
            * excess : mu^ex at each grid
        :param *args: endless possibilities here
        """
        cls.rism_step = step
        cls.resolution = resolution
        # cls.rism_cmd +=  f" -cmd closure={ cls.closure} rism,step={ cls.rism_step}"#f" rism,step={ cls.rism_step}"
        ###
        tmp =  cls.solute_box
        if cls.structure_file_type == '.gro':
            # box is in nm
            convert = (10)/resolution
            cls.grid = [i*convert for i in tmp]
        if cls.structure_file_type == '.pdb':
            # box is in Angstrom
            convert = 1/resolution
            cls.grid = [i*convert for i in tmp]
        ###################################
        #cls.save_command = f' save:{args}'
        cls.save_command = f' save:{values_to_save}'
        for arg in args:
            cls.save_command += arg
        return

    def report(cls,out_file_name:str=None,to_report:str='all',*args):
        """
        function specifies the name of the .log file and
        which params to write out into it
        file name can be specified with  cls.log as well

        :param out_file: name for .log file
        :param to_report: things to write to log file, i would just leave as all
        :param *args: command save strings
        """

        # it can include the path
        if not out_file_name:
            cls.log = cls.structure_file.split(cls.structure_file_type)[0]#+".log"
             #out_file_name
        ####
        cmd_string = " report:"
        cmd_string += f"{to_report}"
        for arg in args:
            cmd_string += f"{arg}"
        cls.to_report = f" {cmd_string}" #{ cls.rism_cmd} {cmd_string}"
        return

    def get_version(cls):
        """
        returns the version by simply calling episol kernel
        from the command line
        """
        temp = subprocess.check_output([f'{ cls.cmd_path}eprism3d --version'],shell=True)
        return ''.join([chr(i) for i in temp[:-1]])

    def get_help(cls,search_str:str):
      """
      searches episol by calling --help from the CLI

      :param search_str: string to search for
      """
      search_str = search_str.strip()
      xx = subprocess.run(["eprism3d","--h",search_str],capture_output=True)
      xv = ''.join([chr(i) for i in xx.stdout[:-1]])
      return print(xv)


    def __str__(cls):
        outstr = ""
        for (key,val) in cls.__dict__.items():
            outstr += f"{key}:{val}\n"
        return outstr

    def test(cls,nt=1,v=1):
        """
        Calls episol and adds -test flag to the CLI
        returns the expected memory usage for the run

        :param v: int(), verbose rating
        :param nt: int(), number of threads to use
        """
        cls.test_args += f" -f {  cls.solute_path+ cls.structure_file} -s {  cls.solute_path+ cls.solute_top}"
        cls.test_args += f" -p {  cls.solvent_path+ cls.solvent_top}"
        cls.test_args += f" -coulomb { cls.coulomb}"
        # cls.rism_cmd += f' -cmd closure={ cls.closure} rism,step={ cls.rism_step}'
        cls.test_args += f" -rc { cls.r_c} "
        cls.test_args += f" -T { cls.T}"
        cls.test_args += f" -log { cls.log}.log"
        cls.test_args += f" -nr { cls.grid[0]}x{ cls.grid[1]}x{ cls.grid[2]}"
        cls.test_args += f" -ndiis { cls.ndiis}"
        cls.test_args += f" -errtolrism { cls.err_tol}"
        cls.test_args += f" -delvv { cls.delvv}"
        cls.test_args += f" -dynamic-delvv { cls.dynamic_delvv}"
        cls.test_args += " -pwd ./" #"~/mnt/f/water_proj"
        cls.test_args += f" -o {cls.log}"
        cls.test_args += f" -cmd closure={ cls.closure} rism,step={ cls.rism_step}"#f" rism,step={ cls.rism_step}"# cls.rism_cmd
        cls.test_args +=  cls.to_report
        cls.test_args +=  cls.save_command
        ###
        cls.test_args += f' -nt {nt} -test'
        subprocess.run([f"{ cls.cmd_path}eprism3d { cls.test_args}"],shell=True)
        cls.test_args = ''

        with open(f"{ cls.log}.log",'r') as f:
          #mem = str()
          for line in f:
            tmp = line.split()
            if tmp[0] == "Memory":
              mem = f'{tmp[5]}{tmp[6]}'
              break
        f.close()
        return mem

    def kernel(cls,nt=1,v=1):
        """
        Calls on EPISOl to perform the 3DRISM calculation

        :param v: int(), verbose rating
        :param nt: number of threads to use
        """
        cls.rism_args += f" -f {cls.solute_path+cls.structure_file} -s {cls.solute_top_path+ cls.solute_top}"
        cls.rism_args += f" -p {cls.solvent_path+cls.solvent_top}"
        cls.rism_args += f" -coulomb {cls.coulomb}"
        # cls.rism_cmd += f' -cmd closure={ cls.closure} rism,step={ cls.rism_step}'
        cls.rism_args += f" -rc {cls.r_c} "
        cls.rism_args += f" -T {cls.T}"
        cls.rism_args += f" -log {cls.log}.log"
        cls.rism_args += f" -nr {cls.grid[0]}x{ cls.grid[1]}x{ cls.grid[2]}"
        cls.rism_args += f" -ndiis {cls.ndiis}"
        cls.rism_args += f" -errtolrism {cls.err_tol}"
        cls.rism_args += f" -delvv {cls.delvv}"
        cls.rism_args += f" -dynamic-delvv {cls.dynamic_delvv}"
        cls.rism_args += " -pwd ./" #"~/mnt/f/water_proj"
        cls.rism_args += f" -o {cls.log}"
        cls.rism_args += f" -cmd closure={ cls.closure} rism,step={ cls.rism_step}"#f" rism,step={ cls.rism_step}"# cls.rism_cmd
        cls.rism_args +=  cls.to_report
        cls.rism_args +=  cls.save_command
        # using unix system is better to run subprocess as
        # argument strings, rather than **args
        # i.e. better "exe.exe -command value" than "exe.exe","command","value"
        # cls.rism_args += f' save:all -nt {nt} -v {v}'
        cls.rism_args += f' -nt {nt} -v {v}'
        subprocess.run([f"{cls.cmd_path}eprism3d {cls.rism_args}"],shell=True)#, cls.rism_args],shell=True)
        cls.rism_args = '' # clear vars so we do not overwrite if reinitializing
        # now check the log file
        with open(f'{ cls.log}.log','r') as f:
          for line in f:
            tmp = line.split()
            if tmp[0][:4] == "RISM":
              out = float(tmp[4])
              step = tmp[2]
        f.close()
        try:
            if out >  cls.err_tol:
                print(f"Failed to reach desired err_tol of { cls.err_tol}")
                print(f"Actual error: {out}")
                print(f"Difference: { cls.err_tol - out}")
                print(f"RISM finished at step {step}")
            else:
                print(f"Calculation finished in {step} steps ")
                print(f"err_tol: { cls.err_tol} actual: {out}\n")
        except UnboundLocalError as exc:
            with open(f'{ cls.log}.log','r') as rr:
                tmp_err_hold = rr.read()
            rr.close
            print("\n\n!It appears your calculation has encountered an error")
            print(f"!Please see the output from the log file ({cls.log}.log)\n")
            print(tmp_err_hold)
            raise exc
        return

    def dump(cls,file_name:str=None,out_name:str=False,list_values:bool=False,value_to_extract:int=1):
        """
        Extracts the compressed .ts4s file and writes the selected value_to_extract to a txt file
        usually you wont use this commnd and this process will be done automatically

        :param file_name: dump file to read
        :param out_name: extract files to this txt file
        :param list_values: return list of saved values
        :param value_to_extract: given the list of values select index to extract
        """
        if not out_name:
            out_name = file_name

        if not file_name:
          file_name = f'{cls.log.split(".log")[0]}.ts4s'

        if list_values:
            thold = ''.join([chr(i) for i in subprocess.check_output([f"ts4sdump -f {file_name} -l"],shell=True)]).split('\n')
            for item in thold:
              print(item)
        else:
          subprocess.run([f"ts4sdump -f {file_name} -e {value_to_extract} > {out_name}.txt"],shell=True)
          cls.extracted_file = f'{out_name}.txt'
        return

    def err(cls,log_file_name:str=None):
      """
      This function reads a log file and returns
      the SCF stdev in an array

      :param log_file_name: name of .log file
      returns an np.array() with shape (1, # steps)
      array index represents the SCF step
      """
      from numpy import array

      if not log_file_name:
          log_file_name = f'{cls.log}'
      with open(f'{log_file_name}.log','r') as f:
          out_arr = []
          for line in f:
              tmp = line.split()
              if tmp[0][:4] == "RISM":
                  out_arr.append(float(tmp[4]))
                  #step = tmp[2]
      f.close()
      #print(out_arr)
      return array(out_arr)

    def reader(cls,file_in:str,laplacian:bool=False,LoG:bool=False,
    convolve:bool=False,sigma:float=1.52,atom_to_select:str="O",file_out:str='out',dx=False):
      """
      This function takes in an uncompressed dump file txt file
      it reads the grid size and shape
      If specified we can save/export to a dx file which can be loaded into pymol/vmd/etc.

      :param file_in: the decompress txt file from our ts4s dump command
      :param file_out: filename for saved dx file
      :param convolve:
      :param sigma:
      :param atom_to_select:
      :param file_out:
      :param dx: write to .dx file, I would reccommend passing to numpy array and using GridData

      .. warning ::
          since the dx file was made by IBM in the 90s
          many nont-so-modern softwares will struggle to read
          dx files with comments and it appears many follow their own
          format specifications
      """
      from numpy import loadtxt,zeros,copy
      from scipy.ndimage import laplace,gaussian_laplace,gaussian_filter

      grid_spacing = [ cls.resolution for _ in range(3)]
      #[i/j for (i,j) in zip( cls.solute_box, cls.grid)]
      # here we choose what column in the txt file to extract
      # cols 1-3 are indices, and then values for O, H, any other elements
      # given in order from the gvv file.
      # for magnesium, this is column 4 (or 5 in python)
      if type(atom_to_select) == int:
          # you can also select your own column
          col_to_select = atom_to_select
      else:
          atom_to_select = atom_to_select.strip().lower()
          if atom_to_select == "o": col_to_select = 3
          if atom_to_select == "h": col_to_select = 4
          if atom_to_select == "mg": col_to_select = 5

      xs,ys,zs = loadtxt(file_in)[-1][:3]
      #x = loadtxt(file_in,usecols=(3))
      x = loadtxt(file_in,usecols=(col_to_select))
      #xs,ys,zs
      shaped = zeros((int(xs),int(ys),int(zs)))
      cont = int()
      # need to numba this
      for zval in range(int(zs)):
        for yval in range(int(ys)):
            for xval in range(int(xs)):
                shaped[xval][yval][zval] = x[cont]#np.linalg.norm(x[cont])
                cont +=1
      if laplacian and not dx:
        return laplace(shaped)
      elif convolve and not dx:
          return gaussian_filter(shaped,sigma=sigma)
      elif LoG and not dx:
          return gaussian_laplace(shaped,sigma=sigma)
      elif not dx:
        return shaped
      if dx:
        with open(f'{file_out}.dx','w+') as outfile:
          outfile.write(f"""object 1 class gridpositions counts     {xs}     {ys}      {zs}
origin 0.0000   0.0000   0.0000
delta  {grid_spacing[0]} 0 0
delta  0 {grid_spacing[1]} 0
delta  0 0  {grid_spacing[2]}
object 2 class gridconnections counts     {xs}     {ys}      {zs}
object 3 class array type double rank 0 items {int(xs*ys*zs)} follows\n""")
          for ind, val in enumerate(shaped.flatten()):
            outfile.write(f"{val:0.5e} ")
            if (ind != 0) and (ind % 3 == 0):
              outfile.write("\n")
        outfile.close()

    def placement(cls,num_waters_to_place:int,atom_to_select='O',radius:float=1.9269073728633292,filename:bool=False,
    grid_spacing=None,write_pdb:bool=False,outname:str='out.pdb',weight:bool=None):
      """
      function places an atom at the (grid) location with the highest
      density, then removes the density surrounding the region according
      to a probe and continues the search until all atoms are placed.
      kind of like placevent. or Ambers/openeye 'blob' method, but those are
      so boring and you can specify the number of atoms you want to place. This
      method is super simple and also naive which means it works.

      :param num_waters_to_place: number of waters to place
      :param atom_to_select: str ( O: oxygen, H: hydrogen, MG: magnesium) int (column of txt file to select)
      :param radius: distance around selected point to omit from remaining placement in Angstrom
      ideal_radius = ((10**3)/(4/3)/(np.pi)/33.3679)**(1/3) based on number density of water
      :param filename: txt file containing density, format is: (columns) x,y,z val_1 (oxygen) val_2 (hydrogen) val_3 (your mixture)
      :param grid_spacing: conversion from array indices to angstrom, units of 1/A, the program automatically converts for you but you can override if need be
      :param outname: string for pdb file
      :param write_pdb: kind of uh, self explanitory, need to update bc its useless, if you specify outname then write_pdb is set to true
      :param weight: numpy array with the same dimensions as your 3DRISM calc. or the filename that you inserted. they is just multiplied together...
      """
      import numpy as np
      import datetime

      if grid_spacing is None:
        # you can overide the grid spacing if need be
        grid_spacing =  cls.resolution
      if not filename:
        filename = f'guv_{cls.log}.txt'

      if type(atom_to_select) == int:
          # you can also select your own column
          col_to_select = atom_to_select
      else:
          atom_to_select = atom_to_select.strip().lower()
          if atom_to_select == "o": col_to_select = 3
          if atom_to_select == "h": col_to_select = 4
          if atom_to_select == "mg": col_to_select = 5

      xs,ys,zs = np.loadtxt(filename)[-1][:3]
      #x = np.loadtxt(filename,usecols=(3))
      x = np.loadtxt(filename,usecols=(col_to_select))
      # need to numba this ######################
      shaped = np.zeros((int(xs),int(ys),int(zs)))
      cont = int()
      for zval in range(int(zs)):
        for yval in range(int(ys)):
            for xval in range(int(xs)):
                shaped[xval][yval][zval] = x[cont]#np.linalg.norm(x[cont])
                cont +=1
      ######################
      inputgrid = np.copy(shaped)
      x = np.arange(0,inputgrid.shape[0])
      y = np.arange(0,inputgrid.shape[1])
      z = np.arange(0,inputgrid.shape[2])
      out_array = [] # need to allocate this mf
      # need to numba this ######################

      for wat in range(num_waters_to_place):
          r_x,r_y,r_z = np.where(inputgrid == np.max(inputgrid))
          r_x,r_y,r_z = r_x[0],r_y[0],r_z[0]
          out_array.append([float(r_x),float(r_y),float(r_z)])
          mask = (x[:,np.newaxis,np.newaxis]-r_x)**2 + (y[np.newaxis,:,np.newaxis]-r_y)**2 + (z[np.newaxis,np.newaxis,:]-r_z)**2  < (radius/grid_spacing)**2
          inputgrid[mask] = -1
      ################################
      if write_pdb:
        x,y,z =  cls.grid
        with open(f'{outname}.pdb','w+') as pdb:
            pdb.write(f"CRYST1    {str(x).ljust(4,'0')}    {str(y).ljust(4,'0')}    {str(z).ljust(4,'0')}  90.00  90.00  90.00 P 1           1\n")
            count = 1
            for val in np.array(out_array)*grid_spacing:#guess2:
                if (atom_to_select == "H") or (atom_to_select == "O"):
                    pdb.write(f"ATOM   {str(count).rjust(4,' ')}  {atom_to_select}    HOH  A{str(count).rjust(3,' ')} {val[0]:8.3f} {val[1]:8.3f} {val[2]:8.3f}\n")
                elif (atom_to_select == "mg"):
                    # FIX THIS!!! somehow gives a 'o' instead of MG???
                    pdb.write(f"ATOM   {str(count).rjust(4,' ')}  {atom_to_select}    MG   A{str(count).rjust(3,' ')} {val[0]:8.3f} {val[1]:8.3f} {val[2]:8.3f}\n")
                else:
                    pdb.write(f"ATOM   {str(count).rjust(4,' ')}  {atom_to_select}    UNK  A{str(count).rjust(3,' ')} {val[0]:8.3f} {val[1]:8.3f} {val[2]:8.3f}\n")

                count +=1

      return np.array(out_array)*grid_spacing

    def select_coords( cls,in_file:str,sele:str,atom_sele:str=None,conv_fact:int=10):
      """
      Select the coordinates of a .gro file and
      return as an array of coordinates

      :param sele: selection string -> resname only so far
      :param in_file: .gro file
      :param conv_fact: convert from nm to grid-bits
      for .gro this is X nm*(10A/1nm)
      """
      import numpy as np
      # this is where we select the selection string
      tmp_string = sele.split()
       # Xnm*(10A/1nm)
      with open(f'{in_file}','r') as r:
          count = int()
          atom_count = int()
          out_dict = {}
          for line in r:
            count += 1
            if count == 2:
              atom_count = int(line.split()[0])
            if count == atom_count+2:
              break # this is the end of the file
            ###########
            if count > 2: # ignore header
              try:
                res_id = line[:5].split()[0]
                res_name = line[5:10].split()[0]
                # there is probably a better way of doing this
                if f"{res_name+res_id}" not in out_dict.keys():
                  # if the residue is not in the dictionary, add it
                  out_dict[f"{res_name+res_id}"] = {}
                else:
                  #print(line[20:28].split()[0])
                  out_dict[f"{res_name+res_id}"][f"{line[10:15].split()}"] = conv_fact*np.array([float(line[20:28].split()[0]),
                                                                                      float(line[28:36].split()[0]),
                                                                                      float(line[36:44].split()[0])])
              except ValueError:
                print(f"ERROR OCCURED AT LINE: {count}")
                continue
      # now we return the x,y,z positions ONLY
      out_array = np.array([])
      for val in out_dict.keys():
        if val[:3] == sele:
          # this uh is a pretty bad way of doing this
          out_array = np.append(out_array,[i for i in out_dict[val].values()])
      #out_array = np.array(out_array)
      #print('out array',out_array)
      """if len(out_array.shape) > 2:
        # this is a bad way of doing this
        y,z,_ = out_array.shape
        out_array = out_array.flatten()#.shape
        out_array = out_array.reshape((y*z,3))"""
      out_array = out_array.reshape((int(len(out_array)/3),3))

      return out_array

    def select_around(cls,rism_grid,in_coords,around:float=5.0):
      """
      function will take an input grid, select the values surrounding the input
      coordinates according to the user, then return the array surrounding the coords
      while the values greater than the cutoff distance are set to np.NaN
      this is so plotting is easier

      :param rism_grid: numpy array of 3D volumetric data
      :param in_coords: positions to select around
      :param around: distance (A) to select around in_coords
      """
      import numpy as np
      conversion =  cls.resolution
      around = around/conversion # must convert A to grids
      rism_grid = np.copy(rism_grid)
      x = np.arange(0,rism_grid.shape[0])
      y = np.arange(0,rism_grid.shape[1])
      z = np.arange(0,rism_grid.shape[2])
      #
      index_grid = np.full((rism_grid.shape[0],rism_grid.shape[1],rism_grid.shape[2]),False,dtype=bool)

      # need to numba this
      for coords in in_coords:
        x_r,y_r,z_r = float(coords[0])/conversion,float(coords[1])/conversion,float(coords[2])/conversion
        index_grid[(x[:,np.newaxis,np.newaxis]-x_r)**2+(y[np.newaxis,:,np.newaxis]-y_r)**2+(z[np.newaxis,np.newaxis,:]-z_r)**2 < around**2] = True
      return np.where(index_grid == True,rism_grid,np.nan)

    def extract_grid(cls,input_file:str,sele:str='guv',out_name:str='out'):
      """
      This function extracts calc. data from the dump file
      by searching for the value corresponding to the selection string
      This way you dont need to list values to extract them.
      You probably wont use this command as it is mainly interal

      :param input_file: .ts4s file you wish to extract
      :param sele: selection string based on .ts4s stored names
      :param out_name: name to write the extracted data to
      """
      assert sele != 'cmd', 'you selected the saved command (cmd)'
      thold = ''.join([chr(i) for i in subprocess.check_output([f"ts4sdump -f {input_file} -l"],shell=True)]).split('\n')
      for val in thold:
        try:
          tmp_str = val.split('@')[0].split()#[1] #.index('guv')
          if tmp_str[1] == sele.strip():
            #print(tmp_str[0])
            value_to_extract = tmp_str[0]
        except IndexError:
          continue
      subprocess.run([f"ts4sdump -f {input_file} -e {value_to_extract} > {out_name}.txt"],shell=True)
          # cls.extracted_file = f'{out_name}.txt'
      return

    def select_grid( cls,input_string:str='guv',coord_array=None):
      """
      select values in array based on the selection input string
      so far selection string is limited to selection of
      grid-values around single residue names only: i.e. around 4 resname LYS
      But we reccommend using the coordinate array input for more in-depth selections
      selection string can include the following key-words
      any output value from 3DRISM, i.e 'guv', 'uuv' or 'coul' etc. etc.
      around 'distance'.
      select grid values around coordinates within specified distance (in Angstrom)

      * get :: get the exact grid value on the input coordinates (i.e. resname or coord_array)
      * resname :: any 3-letter cannonical residue name, upper or lower case
      * 'laplace' or 'laplacian' or 'lap' or 'grad' or 'gradient' or 'del' :: return laplacian of the whole grid
      this selection can be used in tandem with 'around' and 'get' but will always return the laplacian of the
      original unmasked grid, and NOT the laplacian of the selection region.
      * 'convolve' or 'log' or 'laplacian of gaussian' :: return the grid convolved with a laplacian of gaussian (LoG)
      filter. Same specification as above, usse sigma stdev. for gaussian kernel in the LoG filter

      example selection
      ```
      cls.select_grid('LoG of guv with sigma 3 around 4 resname MOL')
      ```
      creates laplacian of gaussian of the g(r) grid with a gaussian std. of 3,
      then selects the region around 4 A of all atoms in the residue named 'MOL'

      parameters
      ----------
      :param input_string: value to select and extract
      :param coord_array: N x 3 array of positons to select around
      """
      from types import NoneType
      from numpy import ndarray,array,where,round,append,float64
      from os.path import exists
      lap_flag = False # to laplacian
      conv_flag = False# to convolve with LoG
      gauss_flag = False # to convolve

      if type(coord_array) == NoneType:
        coord_flag = False
      elif type(coord_array) == list:
        coord_flag = True
        coord_array = ndarray(coord_array)
        # change array into np.array
      elif type(coord_array) == ndarray:
        coord_flag = True

      # these are the possible names to extract
      # we can add more but for now it is unlikely people
      # will want to select weird values, i.e. hlr
      names = {'guv','uuv','ex','ld','coul','huv'}
      # in the future need to add dictionary so people can
      # use more strings, e.g. select g(r) or local density -> guv, ld
      parser = input_string.lower().split()
      #print(parser)
      item = None # this is our selection value i.e. resname
      for name in names:
        if name in parser:
          val = name
          break # can only select one calculation result
      # can override selections pretty easily
      """if 'laplace' in parser:
          lap_flag = True

      if 'log' in parser:
          conv_flag = True
      if 'gaussian' or 'gauss' or 'ld' or 'convolve' in parser:
          gauss_flag = True"""
      #print(parser)
      # base python does not support comparing list with or very well
      #truth = array([name_ for name_ in parser])
      #gauss_flag = (truth.any() == array(['gaussian' ,'gauss' , 'ld' , 'convolve']).any())
      #lap_flag = (truth.any() == array(['laplacian' , 'lap' , 'del' , 'grad' , 'gradient']).any())
      #conv_flag = (truth.any() == 'log')
      gauss_flag = any(name == tru for tru in ['gaussian' ,'gauss' , 'ld' , 'convolve'] for name in parser )
      lap_flag = any(name == tru for tru in ['laplacian','laplace' , 'lap' , 'del' , 'grad' , 'gradient'] for name in parser )
      conv_flag = any(name == 'log' for name in parser)
      # new
      #atom_flag = any(name == 'atom' for name in parser)
      #print(conv_flag,lap_flag,gauss_flag)
      #####################
      if 'sigma' in parser:
          sigma = float(parser[parser.index('sigma')+1])/ cls.resolution
      else:
          sigma = 1.52# Water VdW
      #####################
      if 'around' in parser:
        #print(parser.index('around'))
        dist = float(parser[parser.index('around')+1])
      else:
        dist = None
      # if no distance is specified then select everything
      #####################
      if 'get' in parser:
        get_flag = True
        #item = parser[parser.index('resname')+1].upper()
      else:
        get_flag = False
      #print(get_flag)
      if (dist or get_flag) and coord_flag:
        # if the user includes an np.array
        # of coordinates then these will be our coordinates to
        # select around
        item = coord_array

      if 'resname' in parser:
        # will override coordinate array
        item = parser[parser.index('resname')+1].upper()
      if 'atom' in parser:
          atom_to_select = parser[parser.index('atom')+1]#.upper()
          try:
              atom_to_select = int(atom_to_select)
          except ValueError:
              pass
      else:
          atom_to_select = "O" # default

      ############## Now extract ts4s file
      if not exists(f'{val}_{ cls.log}'):
           cls.extract_grid(f'{ cls.log}.ts4s',sele=val,out_name=f'{val}_{ cls.log}')
          # if the file is already extracted then continue
      # read extracted data into a numpy array
      if lap_flag:
          t_grid =  cls.reader(file_in=f'{val}_{ cls.log}.txt',laplacian=True,atom_to_select=atom_to_select)
      elif conv_flag:
          t_grid =  cls.reader(file_in=f'{val}_{ cls.log}.txt',laplacian=False,convolve=False,
          LoG=True,sigma=sigma,atom_to_select=atom_to_select)
      elif gauss_flag:
          t_grid =  cls.reader(file_in=f'{val}_{ cls.log}.txt',laplacian=False,LoG=False,
          convolve=True,sigma=sigma,atom_to_select=atom_to_select)
      else:
          t_grid =  cls.reader(file_in=f'{val}_{ cls.log}.txt',atom_to_select=atom_to_select)#,laplacian=False,file_out='out',dx=False)
      #############

      if (not coord_flag) and (dist):
        # if we have a distance then that means we have a selection
        # so we select values around our coordinates of the selection item
        coords_ =  cls.select_coords(f'{ cls.solute_path+ cls.structure_file}',item)
        #print(coords_)
        return  cls.select_around(t_grid,coords_,around=dist)

      if (not get_flag) and (not dist):
        # if we dont have a distance that means we dont
        # have a selection and we merely return the entire array
        return t_grid

      if get_flag and (not coord_flag):
        ee = array([],dtype=int)
        #max_x,max_y,max_z = np.float64(t_grid.shape)

        for val in round( cls.select_coords(f'{ cls.solute_path+ cls.structure_file}',item)/ cls.resolution):
          ee = append(ee,[int(val[0]),int(val[1]),int(val[2])])

        for max_dim in float64(t_grid.shape):
            if (ee > max_dim).any():
                # if any of our rounded values is the grid limit
                # then round down
                ee[where(ee > max_dim)] = max_dim-1
        if (ee == 0).any():
            # if any of the returned are rounded to zero, then add one grid
            ee[where(ee == 0)] = 1
        # reshape to x,y,z coords
        ee = ee.reshape((int(len(ee)/3),3))
        #return the total array but only where we have selected
        return t_grid[ee[:,0],ee[:,1],ee[:,2]]


      if get_flag and (coord_flag):
        ee = array([],dtype=int)
        #max_x,max_y,max_z = np.float64(t_grid.shape)

        for val in round(item/ cls.resolution):
          ee = append(ee,[int(val[0]),int(val[1]),int(val[2])])

        for max_dim in float64(t_grid.shape):
            if (ee > max_dim).any():
                # if any of our rounded values is the grid limit
                # then round down
                ee[where(ee > max_dim)] = max_dim-1
        if (ee == 0).any():
            # if any of the returned are rounded to zero, then add one grid
            ee[where(ee == 0)] = 1

        ee = ee.reshape((int(len(ee)/3),3))
        #x[ee]
        return t_grid[ee[:,0],ee[:,1],ee[:,2]]
      else:
        # if we have a distance and coord_array then we
        # return the grid selected around the coord_array
        return  cls.select_around(t_grid,item,around=dist)

    @staticmethod
    def UC(closure):
      """
      Function to get universal correction (UC) based on the closure
      used for RISM calculation. function returns a dictionary containing both the FEP and
      experimental correction constants 'A' and 'B' in the equation:
      \\delta G^{solv} = \\mu^{ex}+'A'*V_m+'B';
      where V_m is partial molar volume
      from the free energy universal correction proposed by:
      David S Palmer, Andrey I Frolov, Ekaterina L Ratkova and Maxim V Fedorov
      http://dx.doi.org/10.1088/0953-8984/22/49/492101
      :param
      """
      # i got bored of writing conditionals and match looks cooler
      match closure:
        case "KH":
           return {"FEP":[-647.348453608648,4.8547480416612],
                   "EXP":[-619.952559990907,-1.47859772642391]}
        case "KGK":
           return {"FEP":[-462.53443482818,8.04130525293397],
                   "EXP":[-435.780764679989,1.67322083808028]}
        case "PSE2":
           return {"FEP":[-687.908213741747,3.5610101387673],
                   "EXP":[-657.653298424423,-2.65897745235407]}
        case "PSE3":
           return {"FEP":[-702.709116407626,3.75516272446305],
                   "EXP":[-671.598836677146,-2.44628209193456]}
        case "PSE4":
           return {"FEP":[-710.201646298877,4.17184421269326],
                   "EXP":[-684.990022127642,-1.17317388291133]}
        case "PSE5":
           return {"FEP":[-714.134748976177,4.40755095859481],
                   "EXP":[-692.678698950017,-0.430203751105637]} # fitted at alpha=3
        case "PLHNC":
           return {"FEP":[-710.548315106323,4.20537805720096],
                   "EXP":[-678.964891475467,-2.0042752246319]}  # fitted at alpha=3
        case "HNC":
          return {"FEP":[-710.548315106323,4.20537805720096],
                  "EXP":[-678.964891475467,-2.0042752246319]}  # HNC is simply copied from PLHNC

    def free_energy(cls,conv:str='kj/mol',fit_value:str='EXP'):
        """
        Return the free energy of the most recent calculation according to the
        3DRISM object
        ====================
        fit_value: string, energy value to return
        options:
        EXP : experimental fitting
        FEP : free energy of pertubation fitting
        ====================
        conv: sting expression
        default output unit is in !!!! in KJ/mol !!!!
        can specify what units you want to convert to
        by specifying the expression. Function will return
        the value based on original unit convversion
        e.g
        "kcal" resolves to taking original free energy value
        in Kj/mol and multipying it by (1/Kj)*(2kcal)*1mol to convert
        to kcal
        ----------- keyword Options: -----------
        kcal, mol , kj, j , joule
        --------- all other standard math symbols allowed -----------

        ====================
        returns:
        float: free energy of solvation default !!!! in KJ/mol !!!!
        \\delta G^{solv} = \\mu^{ex}+'A'*V_m+'B', where V_m is partial molar volume
        """
        ################# Parse the conversion string #################
        def parse_units(G_solv,to_eval_:str='kj/mol'):
            if not to_eval_:
                return G_solv
            to_eval_ = to_eval_.lower()
            kcal = (0.239006/1.000001104) #KJ to kcal
            joule =j = 1000 #
            mol = 6.022e23 #
            kj = kilojoule = 1
            #to_eval_ = 'y*KJ'.lower() #
            if to_eval_ == 'kj/mol':
                return G_solv
            if to_eval_.find('mol') == -1:
                # no mol specified so convert
                G_solv = G_solv*(mol)
                return eval(str(G_solv)+'*'+'('+to_eval_+')')
            elif to_eval_.find('/mol') != -1:
                #mol = 1# due to default  #6.022e23
                return eval(str(G_solv)+'*'+'('+to_eval_+')')
            elif to_eval_.find('*mol') != -1:
                mol = 6.022e23**2# due to default  #6.022e23
                return eval(str(G_solv)+'*'+'('+to_eval_+')')
        ################# ################# ################# #################
        cc = cls.closure
        #assert fit_value == ("EXP" or "FEP"), "you must choose EXP or FEP"
        A,B = cls.UC(cc)[fit_value]

        with open(f'{cls.log}.log','r') as rr:
            for line in rr:
                t = line.split()
                if t[0] == 'total':
                    #out_energies.append(float(t[10])+float(t[8])*A+B)
                    mu_ex = float(t[10])
                    V_m = float(t[8])
                    break
        rr.close()
        return parse_units(G_solv=mu_ex+V_m*A+B,to_eval_=conv)

def select_greater_than(rism_grid,in_coords,around:float,conversion:float):
    """
    Select array values greater than a cutoff
    """
    around = around/conversion # must convert A to grids
    rism_grid = np.copy(rism_grid)
    x = np.arange(0,rism_grid.shape[0])
    y = np.arange(0,rism_grid.shape[1])
    z = np.arange(0,rism_grid.shape[2])
    #
    index_grid = np.full((rism_grid.shape[0],rism_grid.shape[1],rism_grid.shape[2]),False,dtype=bool)
    # TODO
    # need to numba this
    for coords in in_coords:
        x_r = float(coords[0])/conversion
        y_r = float(coords[1])/conversion
        z_r = float(coords[2])/conversion
        # test
        #t_x = (x[:,np.newaxis,np.newaxis]-x_r)**2
        index_grid[(x[:,np.newaxis,np.newaxis]-x_r)**2+(y[np.newaxis,:,np.newaxis]-y_r)**2+(z[np.newaxis,np.newaxis,:]-z_r)**2 > around**2] = True
        #index_grid[t_x,:,:] = True
    out1 = np.where(index_grid == True,rism_grid,np.nan)
    return out1#[np.isnan(out1) == False]

@njit
def select_between(rism_grid,in_coords,around:list,conversion:float):
    """
    Select array values less than a cutoff
    AND greater than a cutoff
    : param: around :: [lo , hi]
    """
    lo = around[0]
    hi = around[1]
    #around = around/conversion # must convert A to grids
    lo = lo/conversion
    hi = hi/conversion
    #
    rism_grid = np.copy(rism_grid)

    sq_lo = lo**2
    sq_hi = hi**2
    #rism_grid = np.copy(rism_grid)
    # pre-allocate, as the grid can be quite large
    t_x = np.zeros(shape=rism_grid.shape[2]) #np.arange(0,rism_grid.shape[0])
    t_y = np.zeros(shape=rism_grid.shape[1]) #np.arange(0,rism_grid.shape[1])
    t_z = np.zeros(shape=rism_grid.shape[0]) #np.arange(0,rism_grid.shape[2])
    #
    t_x[:] = np.arange(0,rism_grid.shape[2])
    t_y[:] = np.arange(0,rism_grid.shape[1])
    t_z[:] = np.arange(0,rism_grid.shape[0])
    #
    out_grid = np.full(shape=rism_grid.shape,fill_value=np.nan)
    #
    for coords in in_coords:
        x_r = float(coords[0])/conversion
        y_r = float(coords[1])/conversion
        z_r = float(coords[2])/conversion
        #
        #for i in range(len(t_z)):
        for i,z in enumerate(t_z):
            #for i in t_x:
            #z = t_z[i]
            #for j in range(len(t_y)):
            #for j in range(len(t_y)):
            for j,y in enumerate(t_y):
            #print(x)
            #for y in t_y[0,:,0]:
                #y = t_y[j]
                #for k in range(len(t_x)):
                for k,x in enumerate(t_x):
                #for z in t_z[0,0,:]:
                    #x = t_x[k]
                    if sq_lo < (x_r - x)**2+(y-y_r)**2+(z-z_r)**2 < sq_hi:
                        #out_grid[i,j,k] = t_position
                        out_grid[k,j,i] = rism_grid[k,j,i]
                        #out_grid[x,y,z] = rism_grid[x,y,z]
                        #else:
                        #out_grid[i,j,k] = np.nan
                        #out_grid[x,y,z] = np.nan
    return out_grid
